subtopic: CUDA / Warp divergence — cost and mitigation
learningObjective: Reason about the performance cost of intra-warp branch divergence and understand which patterns do or do not cause it.
stem: Which statements about intra-warp branch divergence are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: All conditional constructs in CUDA C++ always compile to divergent branches; the compiler never emits predicated instructions, so `?:` in Case D is exactly as slow as the diverging `if/else` in Case A.

Case A causes intra-warp divergence: the warp effectively serializes into two passes (one for lanes 0-15 running `foo`, one for lanes 16-31 running `bar`), so total cost ≈ cost(foo) + cost(bar) for the divergent instructions rather than max of the two.

Case B is not divergent within a warp because the branch condition depends on `blockIdx`, which is uniform across all threads of a block (and hence across each warp); the warp takes one path with no serialization.

Case D (`v = cond ? a : b`) compiled to predicated instructions avoids serialization but may compute both `a` and `b` (each lane keeps the value selected by its predicate), so if `a` and `b` are expensive, predication can be slower than a well-predicted branch.

explanation: A: Classic intra-warp divergence — lanes that take different paths execute those paths serially with the inactive lanes predicated off. B: `blockIdx` is uniform across all threads in a block, so the entire warp evaluates the branch identically; no divergence. C: `?:` often compiles to select/predicated instructions on GPU (`selp.f32` etc.), which is divergence-free but may pay for both sides — well-predicted (uniform-within-warp) branches can beat predication when the two arms differ greatly in cost. D is wrong: nvcc does emit predicated instructions when profitable.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: nvcc uses predication where profitable.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: divergent branches serialize the warp.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: uniform-within-warp branches do not diverge.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: predication trades divergence for possible dual-work.

assumptions: Standard nvcc code generation for control flow.
nonImplications: Does not imply divergence always halves throughput; it depends on the length of the divergent code region.
Does not imply Volta+ ITS eliminates divergence cost; ITS allows independent forward progress but the SIMT-issue-per-warp model still applies.
